questions.question: Profits inside a Stocks & Shares ISA are…
questions.explanation: Gains and dividends inside an ISA are tax-free.

questions.question: Which of these is generally lower risk?
questions.explanation: A global index fund spreads your money across thousands of companies.

questions.question: A trading app gives you a free share. Before you sell it, check…
options: Any minimum holding period in the terms
questions.explanation: Many free-share offers require you to keep the share, or the account, for a set time.

questions.question: Using the Rule of 72, at 6% a year, roughly how long does money take to double?
Fund A charges 1.5% a year, Fund B 0.2%. On £10,000, how much more does A cost per year?
questions.explanation: 1.3% of £10,000 = £130 a year, and the gap compounds over time.

questions.question: £2,000 grows by 7% a year, compounded yearly. Roughly how much after 10 years?
questions.explanation: £2,000 × 1.07¹⁰ ≈ £3,934. Simple interest would only give £3,400.

questions.question: Diversification means…
options: Putting everything in one hot stock
questions.explanation: Spreading your money means one bad pick can't sink you.

questions.question: An index fund aims to…
options: Beat the market by picking winners
Track a market index like the FTSE 100
questions.explanation: Index funds track a market rather than trying to beat it, which usually keeps fees low.

questions.question: Why do long-term investors often sit tight through short-term drops?
options: Markets have historically recovered over long periods, though nothing is guaranteed
questions.explanation: History favours patience, but past performance isn't a guarantee.

questions.question: “Investments can go down as well as up” means…
options: You could get back less than you put in
questions.explanation: Investing carries the risk of losing money.

questions.question: A dividend is…
options: Part of a company's profits paid to shareholders
questions.explanation: Companies may share profits with shareholders as dividends.

questions.question: Pound-cost averaging means…
options: Investing a fixed amount regularly, buying more when prices are low
questions.explanation: Regular investing smooths out the price you pay.

questions.question: Your fund rises 10%, then falls 10%. Overall you are…
Is crypto held on an exchange covered by the FSCS?
questions.explanation: Crypto isn't FSCS protected. If an exchange fails, you could lose everything.

questions.question: Who regulates most UK investment firms?
questions.explanation: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates investment firms. Check the FCA Register before investing.

questions.question: A platform charges 0.45% a year. On £20,000, that's…
An investment promising “guaranteed 20% a month” is…
questions.explanation: Guaranteed high returns are the classic scam promise.

questions.question: A Stocks & Shares ISA protects you from…
questions.explanation: An ISA is a tax wrapper. Your investments can still fall.

questions.question: Your investments grow 6% in a year when inflation is 4%. Your real return is roughly…
questions.explanation: Real return ≈ 6% − 4% = 2%.

questions.question: Before investing, many guides suggest you first…
options: Build an emergency fund and clear expensive debt
questions.explanation: Expensive debt usually costs more than investments earn, and a buffer stops you selling at a bad time.

questions.question: What is a share?
options: A small part-ownership of a company
questions.explanation: Owning a share means owning a small piece of a company.

questions.question: What is a bond?
options: A loan to a government or company that pays interest
questions.explanation: With a bond, you lend money and usually get interest back.

questions.question: Historically, which has given higher long-term returns, but with bigger ups and downs?
questions.explanation: Over long periods shares have usually beaten cash, but with much more volatility, and with no guarantee.

questions.question: A fund's OCF (ongoing charges figure) is…
options: The yearly cost of running the fund
questions.explanation: The OCF is taken every year, so lower is usually better for similar funds.

questions.question: In a fund, “accumulation” units…
questions.explanation: Accumulation units reinvest income. Income units pay it out.

questions.question: Alice and Ben each invest £100 a month at 6% and stop at 65. Alice starts at 25, Ben at 35. Who ends up with more?
options: Alice, by a large margin, thanks to 10 extra years of compounding
questions.explanation: Starting earlier lets compounding work longer. The gap is far bigger than the extra £12,000 Alice paid in.

questions.question: “Timing the market” means…
options: Trying to buy low and sell high by predicting moves
questions.explanation: Even professionals struggle to time markets. Regular investing avoids the guesswork.

questions.question: Selling investments in a panic during a crash usually…
questions.explanation: Selling turns a paper loss into a real one and can mean missing the recovery.

questions.question: “Past performance is not a guide to future returns” means…
options: A fund that did well before may not do well next
questions.explanation: Yesterday's winners can be tomorrow's losers.

questions.question: You invest £1,000. It falls 50%, then rises 50%. You now have…
questions.explanation: £1,000 → £500 → £750. A 50% fall needs a 100% rise to recover.

questions.question: An ETF (exchange-traded fund) is…
options: A fund that's bought and sold on a stock exchange like a share
questions.explanation: ETFs often track an index and can have low fees.

questions.question: Why is putting most of your savings into your employer's shares risky?
options: Your job and your savings depend on the same company
questions.explanation: If the company struggles, you could lose your income and your savings together.

questions.question: A trading app uses confetti, leaderboards and constant notifications to get you trading. The FCA has warned features like these can…
options: Push people into riskier, more frequent trading
questions.explanation: Gamified trading can encourage behaviour that's bad for your returns.

questions.question: Diversifying across countries means…
options: Owning investments in different parts of the world
questions.explanation: Spreading globally reduces dependence on one economy.

questions.question: Before taking a free share offer, what should you check first?
options: The firm is on the FCA Register
questions.explanation: Check the firm is authorised, plus any minimum deposit, holding period and fees after the promotion.

questions.question: What range of value do most people get from a free share?
questions.explanation: The possible range is wide, and most people get the lower end.

questions.question: Should you deposit more than you're comfortable investing to unlock a bonus?
options: No, the value of the share can fall
questions.explanation: Don't deposit more than you're comfortable investing just to unlock a bonus. A free share is still an investment.

questions.question: A crypto exchange fails. Is your money protected by the FSCS?
questions.explanation: There's no FSCS protection if a crypto exchange fails, and no Financial Ombudsman route for many complaints.

questions.question: How fast can crypto prices fall?
questions.explanation: Crypto can swing wildly, with falls of 50% or more happening quickly.

questions.question: Who should you give your crypto wallet recovery phrase to?
questions.explanation: Never share it. Anyone with your recovery phrase owns your crypto.
